title: OSHA construction stairways and ladders practice questions
description: Free practice questions on OSHA construction stairways and ladders (29 CFR 1926 Subpart X). Every answer is explained and linked to the rule text.

questions.question: Under Subpart X, which other subpart contains additional requirements for ladders used on or with scaffolds?

options.D: Subpart E (Personal Protective and Life Saving Equipment)

questions.explanation: Subpart X says "Additional requirements for ladders used on or with scaffolds are contained in subpart L—Scaffolds."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1050, Scope, application, and definitions applicable to this subpart (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: At a personnel point of access with no ramp, runway, sloped embankment or personnel hoist, a stairway or ladder is required where the break in elevation is at least how much?
questions.explanation: A stairway or ladder must be provided "where there is a break in elevation of 19 inches (48 cm) or more, and no ramp, runway, sloped embankment, or personnel hoist is provided."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1051, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Ladders are the only way in and out of a working area. Starting at how many employees must a double-cleated ladder or two or more separate ladders be provided?
questions.explanation: A double-cleated ladder or two or more separate ladders are required "when ladders are the only mean of access or exit from a working area for 25 or more employees." They are also required when a ladder serves simultaneous two-way traffic.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1051, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does Subpart X say about spiral stairways that will not be a permanent part of the structure being built?

options.A: They may be used if they have a handrail on both sides
options.B: They may be used only by one employee at a time
options.D: They may be used only during daylight hours

questions.explanation: "Employees shall not use any spiral stairways that will not be a permanent part of the structure on which construction work is being performed."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1051, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Within what range of angles from horizontal must stairs be installed?
questions.explanation: The rule states: "Stairs shall be installed between 30° and 50° from horizontal."

questions.question: A stairway that will not be a permanent part of the structure must have landings. What is the most vertical rise the rule allows between landings?
questions.explanation: Such stairways need landings at least 30 inches deep and 22 inches wide "at every 12 feet (3.7 m) or less of vertical rise."

questions.question: What is the largest variation in riser height or tread depth allowed in any stairway system?
questions.explanation: Riser height and tread depth must be uniform within each flight, and "Variations in riser height or tread depth shall not be over 1⁄4-inch (0.6 cm) in any stairway system."

questions.question: A stairway has four or more risers. What must it be equipped with?

options.A: Only a sign warning employees to use caution
options.B: A personnel hoist at the top
options.D: At least one handrail and one stairrail system along each unprotected side or edge

questions.explanation: Stairways "having four or more risers or rising more than 30 inches (76 cm), whichever is less," must have "At least one handrail" and "One stairrail system along each unprotected side or edge."

questions.question: Measured from the top of the handrail to the tread surface (in line with the face of the riser at the forward edge of the tread), what height range does the rule set for handrails?
questions.explanation: "The height of handrails shall be not more than 37 inches (94 cm) nor less than 30 inches (76 cm) from the upper surface of the handrail to the surface of the tread."

questions.question: Handrails and the top rails of stairrail systems must withstand, without failure, a force of at least how much applied within 2 inches of the top edge?
questions.explanation: They must withstand "without failure, a force of at least 200 pounds (890 n) applied within 2 inches (5 cm) of the top edge, in any downward or outward direction, at any point along the top edge."

questions.question: A door opens directly onto a stairway, so a platform is provided. The door's swing may not reduce the platform's effective width to less than how much?
questions.explanation: "Where doors or gates open directly on a stairway, a platform shall be provided, and the swing of the door shall not reduce the effective width of the platform to less than 20 inches (51 cm)."

questions.question: Without failure, a self-supporting portable ladder (other than an extra-heavy-duty type 1A metal or plastic ladder) must be able to support at least how much?

options.D: Four times the maximum intended load

questions.explanation: Each self-supporting portable ladder must support "At least four times the maximum intended load," except that an extra-heavy-duty type 1A metal or plastic ladder must sustain at least 3.3 times it.

questions.question: For fixed ladders and for portable ladders other than step stools and extension trestle ladders, how far apart must rungs, cleats and steps be, measured between center lines?

options.A: Not less than 10 inches nor more than 14 inches
options.B: Not less than 2 inches nor more than 4 inches
options.C: Not less than 20 inches nor more than 24 inches
options.D: Not less than 30 inches nor more than 36 inches

questions.explanation: They "shall be spaced not less than 10 inches (25 cm) apart, nor more than 14 inches (36 cm) apart, as measured between center lines of the rungs, cleats, and steps." Step stools and extension trestle ladders have their own spacing rules.

questions.question: A fixed ladder with a total length of climb of 24 feet or more uses self-retracting lifelines. What is the longest interval the rule allows between the required rest platforms?
questions.explanation: One of the permitted options for such fixed ladders is "Self-retracting lifelines, and rest platforms at intervals not to exceed 150 feet (45.7 m)."

questions.question: A portable ladder is used to reach an upper landing surface and is long enough to extend past it. What minimum extension of its side rails above the upper landing surface does the rule set?
questions.explanation: "The ladder side rails shall extend at least 3 feet (.9 m) above the upper landing surface to which the ladder is used to gain access." Only if the ladder is too short for that may it instead be secured at the top to a rigid support, with a grasping device such as a grabrail.

questions.question: A non-self-supporting ladder (not a wood job-made ladder with spliced side rails) is set up for use. The horizontal distance from the top support to the foot must be approximately what fraction of the working length?
questions.explanation: Such ladders "shall be used at an angle such that the horizontal distance from the top support to the foot of the ladder is approximately one-quarter of the working length of the ladder."

questions.question: Who must inspect ladders for visible defects on a periodic basis and after any occurrence that could affect their safe use?
questions.explanation: "Ladders shall be inspected by a competent person for visible defects on a periodic basis and after any occurrence that could affect their safe use."

questions.question: A portable ladder has a broken rung. What does the rule require?

options.A: It may be used until the end of the shift
options.B: It may be used if the broken rung is skipped
options.C: It must be marked as defective or tagged "Do Not Use" (or similar) and withdrawn from service until repaired
options.D: It must be painted with an opaque coating

questions.explanation: Portable ladders with structural defects "shall either be immediately marked in a manner that readily identifies them as defective, or be tagged with "Do Not Use" or similar language, and shall be withdrawn from service until repaired."

questions.question: Apart from the exceptions in 1926.955(b) and (c), when must a ladder have nonconductive siderails?

options.A: Whenever it is longer than 20 feet
options.B: When the employee or the ladder could contact exposed energized electrical equipment
options.D: When it is used on a stairway landing

questions.explanation: "Ladders shall have nonconductive siderails if they are used where the employee or the ladder could contact exposed energized electrical equipment."

questions.question: Which of these is listed as an area in which employees using ladders and stairways must be trained, as applicable?

options.A: How to apply for an OSHA inspection
options.D: The maximum intended load-carrying capacities of ladders used

questions.explanation: Employees must be "trained by a competent person" in listed areas, as applicable, including "The maximum intended load-carrying capacities of ladders used."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1060, Training requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)
